defs.def: a person who is in charge of other people at work and tells them what to do 老板；工头；领班

ex.s: A lunchtime escape allows her to keep a boss from tapping her on the shoulder.
ex.t: 午间逃离让她得以避免老板拍她肩膀。

ex.s: When your boss or professor sends you out to do man-on-the-street interviews for a story, think about the topic and develop a list of about ten general questions relating to it.
ex.t: 当你的老板或教授派你出去为一篇报道做街头采访时，先想想主题，并就此列出大约十个相关问题。

ex.s: It is no surprise that being one's own boss is appealing to many people.
ex.t: 自己做老板对许多人都有吸引力，这不足为奇。

ex.s: "I wanted to experience the freedom of being my own boss," she said.
ex.t: “我想体验自己做老板的自由，”她说。

ex.s: My employees make me a great boss.
ex.t: 是我的员工成就了我这个好老板。

ex.s: The truth is that you are the boss of your career, and it is up to you to decide what you can do and how well you can do it.
ex.t: 事实是，你是自己事业的老板，能做什么、能做到多好，由你自己决定。

defs.def: a person who is in charge of a large organization 总经理；领导
